hints: Convert the ball mass from $200 \text{ g}$ to kilograms and choose a positive direction, noting the ball reverses from $20 \text{ m s}^{-1}$ towards the wall to $10 \text{ m s}^{-1}$ away.
Recall impulse equals change in momentum, $F\Delta t = m(v-u)$, so the incoming and rebound speeds add when the direction reverses.
Calculate $m(v-u)$ with signs to get momentum change in $\text{kg m s}^{-1}$, then divide by the contact time $0.10 \text{ s}$ to get force in $\text{N}$.
walkthrough: Take motion away from the wall as positive. Then initial velocity $u = -20 \text{ m s}^{-1}$ and final velocity $v = +10 \text{ m s}^{-1}$, with contact time $\Delta t = 0.10 \text{ s}$.
Convert mass to SI units: $m = 200 \text{ g} = 0.20 \text{ kg}$.
Use impulse equals change in momentum: $F\Delta t = \Delta p = m(v-u)$.
Substitute with units: $\Delta p = 0.20 \times [10 - (-20)] = 0.20 \times 30 = 6.0 \text{ kg m s}^{-1}$.
Divide by time for average force: $F = 6.0 / 0.10 = 60 \text{ N}$. The unit $\text{kg m s}^{-2}$ is the newton, so the magnitude is sensible.

options.A: This uses only the $10 \text{ m s}^{-1}$ rebound speed, giving $0.20 \times 10 / 0.10 = 20 \text{ N}$. It ignores the change from the incoming $20 \text{ m s}^{-1}$.
options.B: Total velocity change is $10 - (-20) = 30 \text{ m s}^{-1}$, so $F = 0.20 \times 30 / 0.10 = 60 \text{ N}$ away from the wall.
options.C: This uses mass as $200 \text{ g}$ instead of $0.20 \text{ kg}$ and only the rebound speed, giving $200 \times 10 / 0.10 = 20000 \text{ N}$.
options.D: This uses the correct $30 \text{ m s}^{-1}$ change but leaves mass as $200$ instead of $0.20 \text{ kg}$, giving $200 \times 30 / 0.10 = 60000 \text{ N}$.
